->Chapter 13: The Chapter on Peaceful Practices<- <note>original: "sukhavihāra-parivarta"</note>

<margin>K 275 N 180 W 235</margin>
Then <term>Manjushri</term> <gloss>the Bodhisattva of Wisdom</gloss>, the Ever-Young <note>original: "kumārabhūta"; a title indicating his youthful appearance and high spiritual status</note>, spoke to the Blessed One as follows: "O Blessed One, it is difficult, truly most difficult, what these <term>Bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>beings dedicated to awakening</gloss> <term>Mahasattvas</term> <gloss>great beings</gloss> have undertaken out of reverence for the Blessed One. How, O Blessed One, should this <term>Dharma-paryaya</term> <gloss>way of the Teaching</gloss> be proclaimed by these Bodhisattvas Mahasattvas in the future time, in the final age?"

When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One said to Manjushri the Ever-Young: "A Bodhisattva Mahasattva who is established in four qualities, Manjushri, should proclaim this Dharma-paryaya in the future time, in the final age. Which four? Here, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva who is established in his sphere of conduct and his sphere of activity <note>original: "ācāra-gocara"</note> should proclaim this Dharma-paryaya in the future time, in the final age.

And how, Manjushri, is a Bodhisattva Mahasattva established in his sphere of conduct and sphere of activity? When, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva is patient, disciplined, and has reached the stage of self-control; when his mind is free from fear, alarm, or anxiety; and when he is free from envy. And when, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva does not practice by clinging to any phenomenon <note>original: "dharma"</note>, but observes the true nature of things as they are. That which is non-clinging and non-conceptualizing regarding these phenomena is called the sphere of conduct <note>original: "ācāra"</note> of a Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

<margin>K 276 W 236</margin>
And what, Manjushri, is the sphere of activity <note>original: "gocara"</note> of a Bodhisattva Mahasattva? When a Bodhisattva Mahasattva does not serve kings, nor serve, associate with, honor, or visit princes, royal ministers, or royal officials. He does not serve, associate with, or honor followers of other traditions—itinerant mendicants, wanderers, <term>Ajivikas</term> <gloss>a sect of fatalist ascetics</gloss>, or <term>Nirgranthas</term> <gloss>Jain ascetics</gloss>—nor those who are devoted to secular poetry and literature. He does not serve, associate with, or honor those who keep the spells of the materialists <note>original: "Lokayata-mantra-dharakan"</note>, nor does he associate with materialists <note>original: "Lokayatikas"</note>.

He does not associate with <term>Chandalas</term> <gloss>outcastes</gloss>, pugilists, swine-breeders, poultry-breeders, <margin>N 181</margin> deer-hunters, butchers, actors, dancers, or wrestlers. He does not visit other places used by others for amusement and play. He does not associate with such people, except that when they come to him, he preaches the Dharma to them at the appropriate time, doing so without dependence or attachment.

Furthermore, he does not serve, associate with, or honor monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen who belong to the vehicle of the Disciples <note>original: "Shravaka-yana"</note>, nor does he associate with them. He does not frequent the same places as they do, whether in a walking path or a monastery, except that when they come to him, he preaches the Dharma to them at the appropriate time, doing so without dependence. This, Manjushri, is the sphere of activity of a Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

<margin>K 277</margin>
Furthermore, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva does not repeatedly teach the Dharma to women by taking up any signs of attraction, nor does he desire to see women frequently. He does not visit the homes of others, nor does he think he must frequently converse with young girls, maidens, or daughters-in-law, nor does he exchange greetings with them. He does not teach the Dharma to a eunuch, nor associate with him, nor exchange greetings. He does not enter a house alone for alms, unless he is practicing the mindfulness of the <term>Tathagata</term> <gloss>the Thus-Gone One/Buddha</gloss>. If he does teach the Dharma to women, he does so without even the slightest passion for the Dharma <note>the text warns against even spiritualized forms of attraction</note>.

<meta>The bottom of the page contains critical apparatus notes documenting variants such as "very difficult" instead of "difficult" and "rejoices" instead of "associates".</meta>

<summary>The Buddha explains to Manjushri the four qualities required for a Bodhisattva to teach the Lotus Sutra in the future. The text details the proper sphere of conduct and the social boundaries a Bodhisattva must maintain, including avoiding certain professions and avoiding improper contact with women.</summary>
<keywords>Manjushri, Bodhisattva conduct, sphere of activity, ethics, social boundaries, preaching the Dharma, mindfulness of the Buddha</keywords>
